title: Mercedes V-Class air vent
subtitle: Eco-design and life-cycle assessment
deck: Taking a premium air vent apart to find where its footprint hides, then cutting it.
role: Worked with the team on the whole project and led the life-cycle assessment (LCA), the improvement goals and idea generation, and the evaluation of the environmental improvements. The brief covered analysis only, with no development phase.
team: Aimar Arauzo, Mikel Arnao, Ander Martín
tools: IHOBE Climate & Circularity Calculator, MET matrix, weighted decision matrix

hero.caption: Interior of the 2025 V-Class with the round vents and ambient light.

sections.title: Context and brief
paragraphs: The round vent of the 2025 V-Class weighs 127 g and mixes PC+ABS, chrome-plated rings, brass-plated steel rods, TPE seals and an LED ambient-light board, for a 15-year, 250,000 km life. Chrome on ABS cannot be recycled and the parts cannot be separated at end of life.
Goal: quantify the impact and propose redesigns without losing the premium feel.

sections.title: Teardown
paragraphs: Every part was taken apart, weighed and identified to build the inventory.

sections.title: Life-cycle assessment
paragraphs: Cradle-to-grave with the IHOBE calculator. Functional unit: directable airflow and ambient light for one occupant over 250,000 km. Four hotspots appeared:
list: Electronics (17 g) and PC+ABS (92 g) as raw materials
Air freight of the electronics from Taiwan
LED energy in use: 3.75 kWh, about 1.5 L of diesel

sections.title: Improvement goals and ideas
paragraphs: Ideas from eight eco-design strategies were scored on technical and financial viability, environmental benefit and brand motivation. Three action families went forward: A, a more efficient LED (0.6 W to 0.1 W) built in Europe; B, colour-in-mould instead of chrome; C, recycled r-PC+ABS or mono-material PP.

sections.title: Evaluation
paragraphs: Nine concepts were assessed. Mono-material PP cut the carbon footprint by about 85 %; the wireless, efficient LED with road logistics cut the ReCiPe endpoint by about 65 %. Recycled PC+ABS came out worse than expected, probably because of dataset limits.

figures.caption: Reduction of total impact (ReCiPe endpoint) per concept.

sections.title: Result
paragraphs: The final concept combines C2 + A2 + B2: mono-material, ultra-efficient and free of toxic plating. 84 % of the plastic becomes recyclable in a single stream.

sections.title: Reflection
paragraphs: Next steps: a heat-release joint so treatment plants can split rings from the body in one step, an LCA with the electric EQV's energy mix, and certified suppliers instead of generic proxies.
